transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic today?
I've just been feeling incredibly depressed and empty inside, and it's been like this every day for over a year now. I can't seem to shake this heavy sadness, and I just feel completely drained.
Have you had any period of at least 2 months during the past year when your mood felt back to normal, or has it been depressed most days without a long break?

No, I haven't had any breaks at all. It has been completely continuous, every single day, for the last year and two months. I can't remember a single day during this whole time where I felt normal or okay.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Persistent Depressive Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder], but the patient now reports a continuously depressed mood for over 1 year with no symptom-free period of at least 2 months. That pattern supports Persistent Depressive Disorder and makes Major Depressive Disorder less likely because MDD is typically episodic rather than chronic and continuous over such a long duration.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a depressed, empty mood present every day for over 1 year with no symptom-free period of 2 months or more, which is most consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder. The chronic, continuous course argues against Major Depressive Disorder (typically episodic) and Adjustment Disorder (time-limited and tied to an identifiable stressor).
